subject: Commercial structuring for Acme Health private deployment: node-anchored discount vs usage credits
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acmehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement-acme@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercials for Private Deployment - initial ask

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profiles and the unified tooling for private fleets. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concise commercial proposal so we can model costs for finance. Two key levers they want to see split out:

1) A node-anchored license + platform fee (predictable per-site cost)
2) A consumption/usage credit model (token/embedding based) that can be redeemed against overages

We have an 18-month target window and are specifically asking whether you can:
- Offer a meaningful upfront discount tied to a committed number of nodes
- Provide an implementation credit to offset migration services
- Clarify how support tiers map to response times for on-prem SRE escalations

I've attached a short procurement checklist and the initial redlines (acme_redlines.pdf). Can you return two clean options (node-anchored with tiered discount, and blended usage-credit with smaller node commitment) with clear line items for platform fee, per-node license, and support retainer?

Procurement lead for this track is cc'd. Looking to review quotes internally early next week.

Best,
Sara Lim
Director, Cloud Platforms
Acme Health

Attachment: acme_redlines.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial structuring for Acme Health private deployment: node-anchored discount vs usage credits

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the redlines. I'll put two proposal sketches together and loop in Solutions + Commercial Ops. Quick notes up front:

Option A — Node-anchored (predictable):
- Platform fee (monthly): covers control plane, telemetry, and platform features
- Per-node license: annualized; discount tiered by node count (5-15 / 16-50 / 50+)
- Support retainer: Bronze/Silver/Gold response ladders (Silver includes 4 hr P1 response, Gold 1 hr + named oncall)
- Implementation credit: we can offer a lump-sum credit tied to a 12–24 month commit (ask: 18-month preferred)

Option B — Blended (lower node commit, usage credits):
- Lower minimum node commit; consumption credits applied monthly to token charges
- Platform fee reduced proportionally; higher unit cost after credits used
- Support retainer priced per-site with optional on-call add-on

I want to surface one nuance: some customers prefer the simplicity of node-anchored because it maps easily to on-prem capacity planning and auditors like fixed entitlements. Others like the elasticity of the blended model but it requires tighter metering and settlement.

Next steps: David, can you prepare a quick per-node delta for 8/16/32 node configs and a sample blended run-rate that shows break-even at month 6 and month 12? Marissa, can you queue two quote variants in HubSpot (deal id RDW-ACME-2026-1453)?

Sara, can we tentatively schedule a 30-min call Friday to walk the numbers? I can share a draft SOW for the implementation credit mechanics (acme_sow_draft.docx).

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial structuring for Acme Health private deployment: node-anchored discount vs usage credits

Naomi / Sara — jumping in on the capacity and support mapping. High level assumptions I'm using for pricing worksheet (attached):

- Typical Acme workload: 60% chat + 40% embeddings; token distribution favors short-turnaround queries (avg seq len ~128)
- Node sizing: 1 node = 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for our private runtime (config can be scaled horizontal)

For modeling I prepared three scenarios: 8-node pilot, 16-node pilot, 32-node 1st-stage production. Key takeaways from the sheet (rdw_node_pricing_v3.xlsx):
- Node-anchored gives predictable monthly OpEx and is generally cheaper if sustained utilization >55%
- Blended model favors bursty loads; if Acme expects big periodic spikes, credits avoid overprovisioning
- Support tiers: Bronze (business hours), Silver (24/7 P1 triage, 4-hr response), Gold (24/7 + named on-call, 1-hr SLA + quarterly runbooks)

Implementation credit mechanics (proposal):
- We credit up to 20% of first-year platform fee applied as a one-time invoice credit after cutoff acceptance & migration sign-off
- Credit is contingent on 18-month minimum commitment for the node-anchored option; for blended we can split credit across first 6 months as monthly credits

I've attached the pricing workbook and a short support SLA summary. Happy to walk through on Friday — I can bring an SRE to address the runbook/hand-off process.

— David
David Kim
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachment: rdw_node_pricing_v3.xlsx (XLSX, 230 KB)
Attachment: support_tiers_summary.pdf (PDF, 65 KB)

Thanks Naomi and David — this is helpful. Procurement reviewed the two sketches and their current preference is: Option A (node-anchored) if the implementation credit can be structured as an up-front invoice credit and if Gold support can be included for the first 6 months. They also requested we see an 18-month AMOUNTED quote that shows annualized cost and monthly burn.

A couple asks/clarifications from procurement:
- Will the platform fee be invoiced monthly or can we amortize it as quarterly billing?
- For the implementation credit, procurement needs the credit mechanics in writing (they prefer a clause in the SOW or an amendment).
- Legal redlines attached; they want to limit liability carveouts for third-party telemetry collection (see acme_redlines.pdf).

If possible, please send a follow-up with: (1) a clean quote PDF for Option A showing node tiers and the applied implementation credit, (2) an updated SOW with the credit clause, and (3) proposed billing cadence. If we can get that by Monday EOD we can get this into the finance review for the 18-month commit.

Sara
